children: Semiconductor maker Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD, Financials) is expanding its AI infrastructure footprint in Saudi Arabia with a new live deployment with Cisco and HUMAIN.

The platform is powered by AMD Instinct MI355X GPUs, EPYC CPUs and Cisco networking technology to enable GPU-as-a-service applications from model training to inference. The larger investor aspect is scale.
AMD, Cisco and HUMAIN will deploy up to 250 megawatts of new AI infrastructure from 2027, with the broader partnership still targeting up to 1 gigawatt by 2030.

That gives AMD a substantial chance to extend its presence in sovereign AI infrastructure an area where governments and large corporations are spending heavily to construct domestic computer capacity. The deployment also provides AMD with a live reference customer for its latest accelerators at scale.
Cisco also plays into the same buildout with its Silicon One networking technology and 800G optics meant to hook up huge GPU clusters with lower latency.
The big question for AMD is whether projects like these can convert into ongoing accelerator demand and help close the gap with Nvidia in AI computing.
Investors will be watching how fast the Saudi buildout goes from the current deployment to the anticipated 250MW increase in 2027.

title: AMD's Saudi AI Bet Is Scaling Toward 1 Gigawatt
